description: Skelet P15-2 operator abuse-alarm CLI (executable runbook triage, exit-coded)

compatibility.instructions: Does this grain preserve all contracts: one new script plus one new test module plus runbook wiring prose; no route/schema/migration/permission/billing change; evaluator, thresholds, and existing suites untouched; web CI glob auto-wires the new suite? Any changed behavior?

correctness.instructions: Is the CLI factually correct: imports the committed evaluator (same thresholds); JSONL parsing with line/file budgets; --stuck-jobs/--now validation; exit 0/1/2/3 mapping to ok/elevated/critical/invalid; stdout carries the assessment JSON only on success and nothing on failure? Any claim without evidence?

evidence.instructions: Is evidence sufficient: 5 spawned-CLI tests pass (quiet ok, spike elevated/critical, quota attribution plus stuck jobs, malformed exit 3, over-budget exit 3); evaluator suite still green; no hosted-dashboard claim? Any test claim without a run?

reliability.instructions: Any reliability risk: file/line budgets bound resource use; missing/unreadable/invalid files fail closed exit 3; evaluator throws surface as exit 3 with usage; no partial assessment on failure?

scope.instructions: Anything beyond the operator CLI grain: hosted dashboards, paged on-call, R2/S3 backup, signed artifacts, privacy surfaces, or unrelated refactors? Is managed alerting still honestly deferred?

security.instructions: Does the grain weaken any control: no network/model/hosted imports (fs plus committed evaluator only); file path is operator-supplied local read with byte budget; stdout carries codes/counts/workspace IDs only; stderr carries usage plus bounded messages? Any secret or traversal issue?
